How to use this page

Everything below is sorted by distance from our shop at 7900 W. 83rd St. in Bridgeview, which sits about where the city stops and the southwest suburbs start. The closer you are, the easier it is to get a small job looked at on its own. Further out, a whole interior or a full exterior is straightforward and anything smaller is worth a quick phone call first.

Every town has its own page, and it says what the houses there are usually like: how old they are, what that means for the trim and the windows, and what tends to push a quote up or down. A 1941 street in Beverly and a 2000 subdivision in Frankfort are not the same job, and treating them as one is how quotes go wrong.

Housing figures on this page and on every town page are from two sources, named on each page: the U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates, 2019-2023 (tables B25003, B25024, B25034, B25035, B25077). for suburbs and towns, and the Chicago Metropolitan Agency for Planning, Community Data Snapshots 2026, drawing on American Community Survey 2024 estimates. for Chicago community areas. Every dollar figure on this page is a published Census estimate of what homes in the area are worth. None of it is a price for work.

Questions

About where we work

My town is not on the list. Does that mean no?

It means ask. The list is the service area the owner has confirmed, and no town goes on this site as a promise before he makes it. If you are just outside it, call 708-935-4289 and you will get a straight yes or no on the phone rather than a salesman driving out to find out.

Do you actually work in Chicago, or is that just on the website?

The city is real work and it is the south and southwest sides. Bridgeview is a short run from Garfield Ridge, Clearing, Ashburn, Beverly and Mount Greenwood, and that housing is the same brick and plaster as the inner suburbs, so it is the same job. What we will not pretend is that we cover the whole city. A north side call is better served by somebody on the north side, and you will hear that on the phone rather than after a missed appointment.

Why does every town page talk about how old the houses are?

Because it is the most useful thing to know before anybody quotes, and it is the thing most quotes skip. Around here, older usually means plaster instead of drywall, deeper trim to cut in, windows that have been painted a dozen times, and paint from before 1978 underneath it all. Newer usually means big two story walls and tall entries that need staging. Same word, painting, and completely different jobs.

Where do the numbers on these pages come from?

Suburbs and towns come from the U.S. Census Bureau American Community Survey 5-year estimates for 2019 to 2023. Chicago neighborhoods come from the Chicago Metropolitan Agency for Planning Community Data Snapshots, which draw on the 2024 survey. Community areas are used rather than ZIP codes because a single southwest side ZIP covers three different neighborhoods, and a page built on it would be describing an average of places that have nothing in common. Every figure is a fact about the place, not a price for work.

Do you cover the west suburbs?

Not on this site, and that is deliberate rather than an oversight. The confirmed service area is Chicago plus the south and southwest suburbs. Berwyn, Cicero, Riverside, Brookfield, La Grange and Oak Park have been researched and are ready to add, but a page claiming coverage of a town is a promise, and no promise goes on this site before the owner makes it. If you are west and want the work looked at, call and ask.

Ready when you are

Give us a call and we will come and look at it.

Tell us your town and what you want done, and we will set a time to come and see it. You get a real number once somebody has stood in the room, not a guess over the phone. Mike Walsh owns the company and runs the crew, so you are talking to the person responsible for the work.
